subject: Transportation Systems
title: Why Speed Matters for Rail
description: A quick win: understand Why Speed Matters for Rail.

hook.text: Below 100 mph, trains lose to cars on most routes. Above 150 mph, they start beating planes.

buildup.text: The sweet spot is 100 to 500 miles. Too short to fly, too far to drive, perfect for fast trains.

discovery.text: On the Paris–Lyon route, the TGV captured 90% of the combined air-rail market after it launched.

twist.text: Airlines can't compete below 500 miles once security lines, boarding, and taxi rides are included.

climax.text: High-speed rail doesn't need to beat planes everywhere—just on the routes where door-to-door time wins.

punchline.text: Speed didn't just save rail. It redefined where planes make sense.

quiz.question: In what distance range does high-speed rail compete best with air travel?
